resources.string: Phone time: %1$s. Check it before a field session: the session record uses it.
Time between photos in a burst. Default 2 s: a 3 s step caught about 90 % of insect visits (Edwards et al. 2015).
Default 60 s: longer than a typical visit (about 11 s).
Only a square of each photo is saved: side %1$d %% of the short side of the photo, %2$s. Focus and exposure follow the square. Default: the whole short side, in the middle.
Shows the camera view, to point the phone at the flower. Video saves the whole view.
Default 1024 px: enough pixels on a small insect. Never more than the real pixels inside the square.
One video file per clip, 15 frames per s. Default 5 min.
On the Samsung M12, 10 s of video took about 9 MB at 1080p, 7 MB at 720p and 2 MB at 480p.
Default 4 min: the camera rests about 80 % of the time. It is switched off when the break is longer than 30 s. 0 = no break.
Run for some hours from the start

Clock times, for example 06:00-08:00, 17:00-20:00. A window cannot cross midnight: write 20:00-24:00, 00:00-06:00. Default 05:00-21:00: early morning and evening visits count (Toivonen and Humberg 2026).
Default 1 (today). For more days, keep the phone on a power supply.
Set the values, tap Start session, then switch the screen off with the power button. Files are saved in:\n%1$s
Square side (% of the short side of the photo)
Square: %1$d %% of the short side, %2$d px across in the full photo, saved at %3$d px. %4$s, photo %5$s.
This is fewer than the saved side of %1$d px: the square is saved smaller, never enlarged. Make the square larger for more pixels on the insect.
Video %1$s (frames per s: %2$d); the whole view is saved. %3$s.

Drag the square onto the flower with a finger. The triangle marks the top of the saved photos; it follows how the phone is held, and the position at Start counts. The square is saved at once; the session focuses on it at the start of each burst.

Tests with the back camera, without a preview.

One test photo: the camera opens, waits 5 s for the exposure, focuses once, takes one photo and closes.

Speed test (about 3 minutes): photos one after the other, photos from preview frames, short videos, and Camera2 photos.

The camera starts %1$d s after the tap, so you can switch the screen off first. Results are saved in:
%2$s
Working: the camera starts %1$d s after the tap and closes again when the test ends.
FaunaLapse needs the camera permission to take photos. Tap the button again to allow it.
FaunaLapse is running a camera test
The camera closes again when the test ends.
Photos or video on the schedule. Open the app to stop it.
